arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident originating from a spear-phishing email led to the execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The attacker used encoded PowerShell launched from Outlook to drop and execute an unsigned DLL via rundll32, establishing command and control (C2) communication over HTTPS to a known malicious IP (198.51.100.23). Post-compromise activities included host file modification, lateral movement via SMB to a file server, and attempted Kerberos TGT requests. The payload exhibited keylogging, process injection, and scheduled task-based persistence. Detection occurred via IDS signature for C2 traffic, but initial access went undetected by EDR and email security controls.

Malicious DLL (beacon.dll) written to %TEMP% directory.
rundll32.exe loaded beacon.dll from Temp directory.
Hosts file modified to block security domains.
IDS triggered on outbound Cobalt Strike beacon to 198.51.100.23.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from compromised host.
Successful SMB access to file server WS-FIN-050, indicating lateral movement.

title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Office Application

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dll {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory-resident or file-based Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Team"
        malpedia_reference = "https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.cobalt_strike"
        malpedia_version = "20260411"
        malpedia_license = "Creative Commons CC BY-NC-SA 4.0"
        ttp = "T1071.001, T1218.011"
    strings:
        $a = { 60 00 6C 00 6F 00 61 00 64 00 65 00 72 00 } // "loader" in unicode
        $b = "CryptStringToBinary" fullword ascii
        $c = "HttpSendRequest" fullword ascii
        $d = { 75 10 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 64 89 25 } // common beacon assembly pattern
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and any of ($a, $b, $c) and $d
}

arguments.summary: Credential compromise incident initiated via phishing leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment on WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The attacker executed an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, dropped a malicious DLL in the Temp directory, and launched it via rundll32. Hosts file modification and outbound C2 communication to 198.51.100.23 were observed. Lateral movement attempts occurred via SMB and Kerberos. The payload was confirmed as CobaltStrike.Beacon with keylogging, process injection, and scheduled task persistence capabilities.
